title: Run home server chores on a schedule with an agent
summary: A poster says his AI agent on a home server ran 30 days straight, with 12 scheduled jobs handling backups, spending checks, health checks and a weekly email audit.
agent_role: The agent runs 12 scheduled jobs on its own, from nightly backups to a weekly mail audit. The poster set up the schedule.
outcome: Author reports 30 days of uptime with the 12 jobs running.
what_they_did: The poster runs an AI agent on a home server. Twelve scheduled jobs give it work: a 7am system check, a 2:30am backup to a home storage drive, a spending check every three hours, a watchdog every 15 minutes and a Monday email audit.
how_it_went: He reports 30 days of uptime. He says the value comes from the boring jobs never stopping, not from the model.
worth_knowing: The poster credits steady scheduled routines, not model smarts, for making the agent useful.
prompt: Help me set up recurring jobs for you on my home server. Propose a schedule for: a morning check that my services are running, a nightly backup of [folders] to [backup drive], a check on my [API or subscription] spending every few hours, a watchdog that alerts me if something stops, and a weekly audit of my email for [what to look for]. Show me the schedule and commands and wait for my approval before installing anything.

curation.rationale: A genuine home-server agent running scheduled chores for 30 days with named jobs, but light on tools and results.
